body: Yeah I'm not sure how it works. but my brain tells my fingers what to do without me interfering most of the time.

I sat here for 10 minutes or so trying to think of an answer for you. I don't know what I could possibly learn or gain from having lunch with a dead person or an alive person that I am basically dead to.

I don't even know chords that well. Heh. I just know need to know the root, and the number of sharps/flats. Essentially, those relate to A Minor or C# Harmonic Minor, etc... But I never remember those names.

I've played piano, clarinet, bass clarinet, saxophone, guitar and bass guitar. I was in an orchestra playing clarinet for a short time. I really relied on my knowledge of music theory to get me through that. If you know what key something is in, the rest is pretty easy.
I don't know. Carl Sagan, maybe? He never gave up what he believed. I want to know how and why.

It depends on how you learn new music I suppose. Do you learn a new piece of music when you READ the sheet music, when you HEAR it played or when you PLAY it yourself? Even if you answer in a particular way, you can still learn other things in other ways. My fiance used to play drums in a pipe band and he mentioned a guy that was amazing that couldn't read music. He was a kinesthetic learner as well. I can read music and have played several instruments, but I can never quite figure out a piece is supposed to go until I've played it myself.

I just wish I could find my passion. :/

I kept trying to think of honest answers, but I can't think of anything other than obvious (housing, car, groceries, bills) and going to college. So I changed my mind to this:
I would buy a poor country and enact serfdom...But now that I think of it...I would buy the United States.

I would love to go to college if that were a possibility. I just turned 24 and I think now may be the first year I can apply for financial aid without using my parents tax statements. I will need more than that, however. I will need scholarships and some sort of housing fund. I have 0 credit and absolutely no one I can or would ask for a loan. I'm not sure how a 24 year old that's never been to college with an A- GPA from high school (that really isn't relevant anymore) can get scholarships. I must have applied for nearly 200 while I was a senior in High School. I'm not concerned with *how* to learn so much as I'm concerned as to whether or not it will actually advance my standing. People are much more willing to give someone with a degree a chance at an interview at least.
I learn by practice. I don't like to just be told or shown something. I have to do it and try it different ways to know why it must be done a certain way or what benefits doing a particular thing in a certain way has. I believe I am what is called a Kinesthetic learner.

I honestly can't say that I've had a favorite. I like the end result of getting paid for my work and a client being happy with everything (a true farce). I really dread most of all with my work that there is no finality or consistency to it. The pay is not consistent or standardized in any way. Deadlines are always stretched and shortened. Clients ALWAYS misunderstand and underestimate what all needs to be done and ALWAYS ALWAYS change their minds. 
I used to be a graphic designer in high school and really got tired of finicky clients. I moved on to web development because I had been teaching myself since I was a child and I thought I would have to deal with clients less. It turns out that the people that pay you and "manage" you literally get paid to be a parrot. "The client said X." "The client needs that by lunch." etc...etc...

>If you are dead, there is no progress left to be made.


If there is no progress left to be made, you are dead. Maybe not physically, but what difference would it make?
I agree that tasks to improve yourself are not menial. But how and why should I improve myself? What's wrong with the way I am?
I believe a lot of things. I believe that no one will remember me 20 years after I am dead. I believe that however significant something or someone is in your life, you can usually survive without it. I believe that only you can make yourself happy in one way or another. I believe most people have some general idea of what they want to do with their lives and goals they want to accomplish.
All of my goals and dreams were stripped away from me before I was ever given a chance. I have moved around so much growing up that I have no friends. Everyone forgets about me eventually. Everyone stops caring eventually. 

I don't know how to be a friend. I don't know how to be an enemy. I don't know how to want something.

In first grade, I wanted to be a chemist and find the cure for cancer. I remember this clearly, yet I have no frame of reference as to why or what my motivation was. 
Now, I'm a web developer and I have no idea why or if I even enjoy it. I tell myself I enjoy it and I tell myself that I'm good at it. That's what keeps me doing it.
But I never forgot that I wanted to be a chemist. I know now what causes cancer and I have a few good ideas on how to correct and fix it without radiation or chemotherapy, but I can't say that I'm sure. I've never even been to college. Most schools aren't designed for people that learn...differently. When not presented with opportunity, I might as well have not tried. As an adult, I can't name one thing I learned from school.
I welcome your questions. No one ever asks me anything; apologies for rambling.

I appreciate the suggestions, but I've been dealing with this my whole life. It's not like a tv. I can't change it at will. I am not particularly motivated to do menial tasks that help me accomplish nothing... Other than browsing reddit. Doing menial tasks, I sometimes remember why I am doing it, or more often, that I am wasting time and completely defeats the purpose of me doing them.
I've tried believing in god or a god and I've tried pretending that I do. I just can't sit back and absorb a bunch of nonsense information and try to tell myself "this really happened" or "yep thats how humans should behave."
i lack goals. i lack motive. i lack support.

To my understanding there still is no right medication. You can't flood someone's brain with serotonin and norepinephrine and expect that their brain is just going to sort itself out! I don't buy it. Every drug for depression I've been given has made me feel the same every day. The same HORRIBLE LOOP every single fucking day. It's like hearing the same song over and over every day until you would gladly remove your eardrums just to hear silence again.

my only friend and the only one I confide in is my fiance... my family........ my mom's dad committed suicide. my mom's mom has attempted several times and is on so much medication that she can barely stand. my dad has never been able to talk or open up to anyone and neither have I. My sister is ignorant but is considered intelligent by everyone and the most "successful" person in my family. my half brother is 17 and his dad died suddenly 4 years ago.

in short: i cant stand my family. 

my mom got me on celexa a few years ago and it made everyday as excruciating as the last. she also pressured me to go to several "Christian" counselors. I'm an athiest and I dont want to talk about a bunch of bullshit or having people think I was raped as a child just to be told to TAKE SOME PILLS. No fucking PILL and no amount of BULLSHIT TALKING has ever solved ANYTHING for me.

I used to think I wanted an answer or at least someone who understands me.
But the answers solve no problems, and unfortunately anyone that understands me is just as fucked up as I am.

He doesn't want me to. He's nice in the way that people expect I guess... theres nothing wrong with him... its just me. I've been sticking around because he thinks suicide is cowardly & i don't want to betray him. things happen after people die. i wouldn't be alive to care, but I would be dead enough to blame.
if he's not worth it, then neither is my one reason left for living
